note: Re-judged 2026-10-26 by an independent auditor who authored none of the change, after 394bd1e802 and 180b306ffa (spec-bgp-rs-replacement-on-withdrawal). RFC 8654 Section 5: "Similarly, any speaker that treats an improper BGP Extended Message as a fatal error MUST follow the error-handling procedures of [RFC4271]." RFC 4271 Section 6 requires the invalid routes of the closed connection be withdrawn or replaced by new best routes. relay_recovery.go oweDeparture now requires the departure to name its session generation (refusing generation 0 with an error) and owes a non-ADD-PATH key only when departedOwner holds: same source, entry.owner.generation <= the departed generation, and the owner no longer current. This narrows a departure to the routes of the session that actually closed; a newer session's route was never one of the RFC 4271 Section 6 invalid routes, so the narrowing is what the RFC asks. The generation reaches the engine on the real path: rr.go and rs/server_handlers.go pass StructuredEvent.SessionGeneration as recovery-generation, and update_text.go recoveryFromMeta sets NLRIBatch.RecoveryGeneration. All seven tagged units are byte-identical; TestRFC8654FatalLengthReleasesInstalledRoutes and TestRFC8654FatalLengthReelectsAlternateBest (positives) still require the closed session's routes released and the alternate re-elected, the negatives still require a valid-length message leave the session and routes intact and an over-length one take the NOTIFICATION path; revert records on notifyPeerClosed, emitPurgedWithdraws, readAndProcessMessage, readAndProcessCoalesced and ValidateLengthWithMax verify. Reactor and message TestRFC8654* green at HEAD in an export. Verdict unchanged: enforced. Earlier judgements are in this file's git history.
